script: I left 100€ in my car, then my SIL's boyfriend stole everything.. I was driving to the grocery store, pulling out 250 euros for the trip, but only spent 150. I left the rest—about 100 euros—stashed in my car. No one knew until my sister‑in‑law (SIL) asked for my car key to grab her boyfriend (BF) from the station. She was fine, we had dinner, everything looked good. I felt like the ultimate good guy, right? The next morning, I headed to the watch shop, hoping to get a quick service. The shop only had 30 euros on the counter, so I realized my car must have been missing the other 70. I came home, told my wife, and she said maybe I'd dropped some cash at the grocery store. I had the receipts, and it didn't add up. I didn't buy it. Fast‑forward to a week later, we're all at the beach house for vacation. I paid for groceries, wine, and even gave SIL a "vacation check" so they could cover gas. The only thing they had to pay for was fuel. The BF and I were going to play tennis while my wife and SIL headed to the beach. I set up my work computer in front of my wallet, camera on, Teams open, and a pointless Excel sheet on the screen. I told the BF I'd step out for a bathroom break. When I came back, my wallet was slightly moved—nothing dramatic, so I ignored it. Later that night, after everyone was in bed, I checked the recording. The BF had taken 60 euros from my wallet. The same pattern—he'd only been around when the money was missing. I told my wife the next day. She laughed and said I was just making a scene. She thought I was overreacting, that I was the real jerk for "baiting" him. So, bestie, am I the jerk for setting him up to steal? And should I show my wife the clip or keep it to myself?
